posts.body:
Every Vote Counts
​
Plot
​
Amonena, a country with a very strange constitution.
Due to a strange loophole in Amonena's constitution, a cat has been elected as their head of state. When that law was passed, nobody ever thought that someone would nominate an animal as Prime Minister, and when the cat was sworn in, nobody seemed to care. However, things have now gone downhill in the corridors of parliament.
Now nobody can see the Prime Minister, they can only see it's deputy, Weston. The person who nominated the cat in a moment of apathy has also realised their mistake, and decides to head to parliament to talk with the leader of the opposition, Penny Bradelgast. Simply to offer their services... of course, they'd never tell Miss. Bradelgast that THEY were the one who nominated that cat in the first place!
Recruit a diverse range of characters, from all walks of life
​
Recruit politicians, bartenders, hair stylists, wizards, and even a lady vampire and a mermaid! 20 recruitable characters in all are located throughout the country of Amonena. Each giving their own skills to the party. Too many to list here, but here are the few who you'll no doubt come across during the course of the game.
Penny Bradelgast:
The leader of the opposition party in Amonena. She's willing to accept all the help she can get to try to get that "cat" out of office.
Isaac:
Runs "The Geek Zone" in Aerina. A nerd and proud of it, his skills prove to be invaluable when Penny and the hero are trying to gain access into the government data centre, north of Cordelia.
Claire:
The administrator at the hydro-electric dam north of Bergaln. She is in need of help after Weston's bunch undertakes some sabotage work at the dam, which they would pin down to shoddy infrastructure and under-funding.
Spoiler:
Regarding Circe and the Aviettes - An explanation
Circe and the Aviettes:
The Aviettes were a race invented  for my remakes (which were eventually removed) for my RM2K3 project "A Celestial Weapon". Invented by the amoral scientist James Hawser through genetic experiments, they have spectacular physical strength, but are gentle and kind-hearted. Probably the biggest blunder which Dr. Hawser didn't see coming was that even though he removed the Y chromosome to keep a handle on their numbers, it soon became apparent that they could reproduce by other means.
- A reference to Jurassic Park.
​
Every Vote Counts can be downloaded at itch-io:
https://moonwolfv.itch.io/every-vote-counts
Scenes from the game:
Note: I took some screenshots before I changed the font to Arial part way through making the game. That's why the font differs from screenshot to screenshot.
​
A joke that if Paco's is selling Mexican cuisine, then this must be located somewhere on earth, right?
I had a lot of complaints on rpgmaker.net where this game was originally hosted, that the puzzles in the data centre were a bit of a "running into a brick wall" moment. I worded it differently to make it easier to find your way through.
It's strange how this somewhat shy archivist's leadership skills show themselves as soon as the country is plunged into a crisis.
Came up with this idea when I ended up earning more Battle Points than I needed. Rather than it becoming worthless, I thought why not have an option where you can convert it into more money for yourself?
If you've read the spoilers about Circe and the Aviettes, you'll know exactly what's going on here. If you're not thinking carefully, this battle can wind up being particularly ugly.
And a fun little nod to the original "The Sims" by Maxis / Electronic Arts (EA): It seems that a certain squatter actually had skills as a software developer she simply didn't know about until she received Pandora's and Cassandra's help.
